The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 78, verses 37–40:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Most Merciful﴾. Ibn Mas'ud, Nafi', Abu 'Amr, Ibn Kathir, and Zayd (on the authority of Ya'qub), and al-Mufaddal (on the authority of 'Asim), read (رَبُّ) with a *damma* (raf') as a new sentence (isti'naf), with (الرَّحْمَنُ) as its predicate. Or it may mean: "He is the Lord of the heavens," and (الرَّحْمَنُ) would then be a second subject (mubtada' thani). Ibn 'Amir, Ya'qub, and Ibn Muhaysin all read both with a *kasra* (khafd), as an adjective (na't) of His saying, ﴿a reward from your Lord﴾, meaning: "a reward from your Lord, the Lord of the heavens, the Most Merciful." Ibn 'Abbas, 'Asim, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i read (رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ) with a *kasra* as an adjective, and (الرَّحْمَنُ) with a *damma* as a beginning (ibtida'), meaning: "He is the Most Merciful." [This reading was mentioned by al-Qurtubi and Ibn 'Atiyyah, who did not mention the reading of 'Asim with a *kasra* in both places. It is the narration of Hafs, and Abu Hayyan and al-Alusi mentioned it. Thus the readings on 'Asim's authority are three: a *damma* in both places, a *kasra* in both places, and a *kasra* on (رَبِّ) with a *damma* on (الرحمن).] Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading and said: "This is the most balanced of them: the *kasra* on (رَبِّ) because it is near His saying ﴿from your Lord﴾, so that it is an adjective of it, and the *damma* on (الرَّحْمَنِ) because it is further from it, as a new sentence, whose predicate is ﴿they will not have the power to address Him﴾, meaning they will not have the power to ask Him except concerning what He has permitted them." Al-Kisa'i said: "They will not have the power to address Him concerning intercession except with His permission." It was also said: the (خِطَاب) is speech, meaning they will not have the power to address the Lord, glorified is He, except with His permission. Its evidence is His saying: ﴿No soul shall speak except by His permission﴾ [Hud: 105]. It was also said: He meant the disbelievers, who will not have the power to address Him, but as for the believers, they will intercede. I (al-Qurtubi) say: after they have been given permission, for His saying: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ and His saying: ﴿On that day intercession will not benefit except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and whose word He approves﴾ [Ta-Ha: 109].

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows﴾. (يَوْمَ) is in the accusative as an adverb of time (zarf), meaning: on the day when they will not have the power to address Him is the day when the Spirit stands. Scholars differed concerning "the Spirit," with eight opinions:

The first: it is an angel among the angels. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Allah has created no creature after the Throne greater than it. When the Day of Resurrection comes, it will stand alone in a row, and all the angels will stand in a row, so the greatness of its creation will be like their rows." Something similar is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The Spirit is an angel greater than the seven heavens, the seven earths, and the mountains. It stands opposite the fourth heaven [in another copy: the seventh heaven], and glorifies Allah every day with twelve thousand glorifications. Allah creates from each glorification an angel, so it comes on the Day of Resurrection alone in a row, and the rest of the angels in a row."

The second: it is Jibril, peace be upon him. This was said by al-Sha'bi, al-Dahhak, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. From Ibn 'Abbas: "Beneath the right of the Throne is a river of light, like the seven heavens, the seven earths, and the seven seas. Jibril enters it every morning before dawn and bathes, so he increases in light upon his light, in beauty upon his beauty, and in greatness upon his greatness. Then he shakes himself, and Allah creates from every drop that falls from his feathers seventy thousand angels. Of them, seventy thousand enter the House that is Frequented (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur) each day, and seventy thousand enter the Ka'bah, and they do not return to them until the Day of Resurrection." Wahb said: "Jibril, peace be upon him, stands before Allah, the Exalted, his limbs trembling; Allah creates from every tremor a hundred thousand angels. So the angels are in rows before Allah, the Exalted, with their heads bowed. When Allah permits them to speak, they say: 'There is no god but You.' This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows; none shall speak except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted to speak, and he says what is right﴾," meaning the words: "There is no god but You."

The third: Ibn 'Abbas narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: [The Spirit in this verse is a host of the hosts of Allah, the Exalted. They are not angels; they have heads, hands, and feet, and they eat food.] Then he recited: ﴿On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows﴾, meaning these are a host and those are a host. This is the view of Abu Salih and Mujahid. According to this view, they are a creation in the form of the children of Adam, like people but not people.

The fourth: they are the noblest of the angels. This was said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

The fifth: they are guardians over the angels. This was said by Ibn Abi Najih.

The sixth: they are the children of Adam. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. So the meaning is "those possessing spirits" (dhawu al-ruh). Al-'Awfi and al-Qurazi said: "This is something Ibn 'Abbas used to conceal. He said: 'The Spirit is a creation of Allah's creation in the forms of the children of Adam, and no angel descends from the heaven without being accompanied by one of the Spirit.'"

The seventh: the spirits of the children of Adam will stand in a row, and the angels will stand in a row, and that is between the two blasts, before they are returned to the bodies. This was said by 'Atiyyah.

The eighth: it is the Qur'an. This was said by Zayd ibn Aslam, who recited: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit by Our command﴾.

(صَفًّا) is a verbal noun (masdar), meaning they will stand in rows (صُفُوفًا). A verbal noun may refer to the singular and the plural, like (العَدْل) and (الصَّوْم). The day of the festival is called "the Day of the Row" (يوم الصف). He said in another place: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, row upon row﴾ [al-Fajr: 22]. This indicates rows, and this is the time of the presentation and the reckoning. Al-Qutabi and others said this. It was also said: the Spirit stands in one row and the angels in another, so they are two rows. It was also said: all of them stand in one row. (لا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ), meaning they will not intercede except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted in intercession, and (وَقَالَ صَوَابًا), meaning "what is right," said al-Dahhak and Mujahid. Abu Salih said: "There is no god but Allah." al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "They will intercede for whoever said: 'There is no god but Allah.'"

The root of (الصَّوَاب) is correctness (السَّدَاد) in speech and action. It is from (أَصَابَ يُصِيبُ إِصَابَةً), like (الجَوَاب) from (أَجَابَ يُجِيبُ إِجَابَةً). It was also said: (لَا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ), meaning the angels and the Spirit who stood in rows, will not speak out of awe and reverence, except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted in intercession. And they have spoken what is right, for they affirm the oneness of Allah, the Exalted, and glorify Him. Al-Hasan said: "On the Day of Resurrection the Spirit will say: 'No one enters Paradise except by mercy, and no one enters the Fire except by deeds.'" This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and he says what is right﴾.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is the true day﴾, meaning the day that is certain and will occur. ﴿So whoever wills, let him take a way to his Lord as a return﴾, meaning a place of return through righteous deeds, as if when he does good he brings himself back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and when he does evil he removes himself from Him. This meaning is reflected in His saying, peace be upon him: [And all good is in Your hands, and evil is not attributed to You]. Qatadah said: (مَآبًا) means a way (سَبِيلًا).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾. It addresses the disbelievers of Quraysh and the polytheists of the Arabs, because they said: "We will not be resurrected." The punishment is the punishment of the Hereafter, and everything that is coming is near. Allah, Exalted is He, has said: ﴿As if, on the day they see it, they had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46]. al-Kalbi and others said this. Qatadah said: it is the punishment of this world, because it is the nearer of the two punishments. Muqatil said: it is the killing of Quraysh at Badr. The more apparent view is that it is the punishment of the Hereafter, which is death and the Resurrection, because whoever dies has had his resurrection. If he is among the people of Paradise, he sees his seat in Paradise; if he is among the people of the Fire, he sees disgrace and humiliation. This is why He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿On the day when a man will see what his hands have sent forth﴾.

[He specified the time of that punishment, meaning: We have warned you of a near punishment on that day, which is the day when a man will see what his hands have sent forth, meaning he will see it.] It was also said: "he looks at what he has sent forth," so the preposition (إِلَى) was omitted. (الْمَرْءُ) here, according to al-Hasan, means the believer, meaning he finds for himself a deed. As for the disbeliever, he finds no deed for himself, so he wishes he were dust. When He said: ﴿the disbeliever says﴾, it became known that He meant the believer by (الْمَرْءُ). It was also said: (الْمَرْءُ) here refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf and 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'it. The disbeliever in ﴿the disbeliever says﴾ is Abu Jahl. It was also said: it is general for every person who, on that day, sees the recompense for what he earned.

Muqatil said: the verse ﴿on the day when a man will see what his hands have sent forth﴾ was revealed concerning Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi, and ﴿the disbeliever says: "Would that I were dust!"﴾ was revealed concerning his brother al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Asad.

Al-Tha'labi said: "I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: 'The disbeliever here is Iblis, because he criticized Adam for being created from dust, and boasted that he was created from fire. When on the Day of Resurrection he sees what Adam and his children have of reward, ease, and mercy, and sees what he is in of hardship and punishment, he wishes he were in Adam's place, so he says: "Would that I were dust!"'" He said: "I saw this in one of the tafsir books of al-Qushayri, Abu Nasr." It was also said: meaning Iblis says: "Would that I had been created from dust and had not said, 'I am better than Adam.'"

Ibn 'Umar narrated: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be stretched like a hide, and the beasts, cattle, and wild animals will be gathered. Then retaliation will be established among the animals, until the hornless sheep is avenged against the horned sheep by its butting. When the retaliation among them is finished, it will be said to them: 'Become dust!' At that point the disbeliever says: 'Would that I were dust!'" Something similar is narrated from Abu Hurayrah and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with them. We have mentioned it in our book al-Tadhkirah, concerning the states of the dead and the affairs of the Hereafter, in an excellent manner, and praise be to Allah.

Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas mentioned: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Nafi' told us, who said: Salamah ibn Shabib told us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq told us, who said: Ma'mar told us, who said: Ja'far ibn Burqan al-Jazari informed me, on the authority of Yazid ibn al-Asamm, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Indeed Allah, Exalted is He, will gather all creation, every beast, bird, and human. Then it will be said to the cattle and the birds: 'Become dust!' At that point the disbeliever says: 'Would that I were dust!'"

Others said: ﴿Would that I were dust!﴾, meaning: "I was not resurrected," as He said: ﴿Would that I had not been given my record﴾ [al-Haqqah: 25]. Abu al-Zinad said: "When judgment has been passed among the people, and the people of Paradise have been commanded to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire, it will be said to the rest of the nations and to the believing jinn: 'Return to dust!' So they return to dust, and at that point the disbeliever, seeing them, says: 'Would that I were dust!'" Layth ibn Abi Sulaym said: "The believing jinn return to dust." 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, al-Zuhri, al-Kalbi, and Mujahid said: "The believing jinn are around Paradise, in its outskirts and courtyards, and they are not within it." This view is the most sound. Its explanation has already passed in surah al-Rahman [see vol. 17, p. 169], and that they are under obligation: they are rewarded and punished, so they are like the children of Adam. And Allah knows best what is correct.

Ibn 'Amir, Ya'qub, and Ibn Muhaysin all read both with a *kasra* (khafd), as an adjective (na't) of His saying, ﴿a reward from your Lord﴾, meaning: "a reward from your Lord, the Lord of the heavens, the Most Merciful." Ibn 'Abbas, 'Asim, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i read (رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ) with a *kasra* as an adjective, and (الرَّحْمَنُ) with a *damma* as a beginning (ibtida'), meaning: "He is the Most Merciful." [This reading was mentioned by al-Qurtubi and Ibn 'Atiyyah, who did not mention the reading of 'Asim with a *kasra* in both places. It is the narration of Hafs, and Abu Hayyan and al-Alusi mentioned it. Thus the readings on 'Asim's authority are three: a *damma* in both places, a *kasra* in both places, and a *kasra* on (رَبِّ) with a *damma* on (الرحمن).] Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading and said: "This is the most balanced of them: the *kasra* on (رَبِّ) because it is near His saying ﴿from your Lord﴾, so that it is an adjective of it, and the *damma* on (الرَّحْمَنِ) because it is further from it, as a new sentence, whose predicate is ﴿they will not have the power to address Him﴾, meaning they will not have the power to ask Him except concerning what He has permitted them." Al-Kisa'i said: "They will not have the power to address Him concerning intercession except with His permission." It was also said: the (خِطَاب) is speech, meaning they will not have the power to address the Lord, glorified is He, except with His permission. Its evidence is His saying: ﴿No soul shall speak except by His permission﴾ [Hud: 105]. It was also said: He meant the disbelievers, who will not have the power to address Him, but as for the believers, they will intercede. I (al-Qurtubi) say: after they have been given permission, for His saying: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ and His saying: ﴿On that day intercession will not benefit except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and whose word He approves﴾ [Ta-Ha: 109].

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows﴾. (يَوْمَ) is in the accusative as an adverb of time (zarf), meaning: on the day when they will not have the power to address Him is the day when the Spirit stands. Scholars differed concerning "the Spirit," with eight opinions:

The first: it is an angel among the angels. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Allah has created no creature after the Throne greater than it. When the Day of Resurrection comes, it will stand alone in a row, and all the angels will stand in a row, so the greatness of its creation will be like their rows." Something similar is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The Spirit is an angel greater than the seven heavens, the seven earths, and the mountains. It stands opposite the fourth heaven [in another copy: the seventh heaven], and glorifies Allah every day with twelve thousand glorifications. Allah creates from each glorification an angel, so it comes on the Day of Resurrection alone in a row, and the rest of the angels in a row."

The second: it is Jibril, peace be upon him. This was said by al-Sha'bi, al-Dahhak, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. From Ibn 'Abbas: "Beneath the right of the Throne is a river of light, like the seven heavens, the seven earths, and the seven seas. Jibril enters it every morning before dawn and bathes, so he increases in light upon his light, in beauty upon his beauty, and in greatness upon his greatness. Then he shakes himself, and Allah creates from every drop that falls from his feathers seventy thousand angels. Of them, seventy thousand enter the House that is Frequented (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur) each day, and seventy thousand enter the Ka'bah, and they do not return to them until the Day of Resurrection." Wahb said: "Jibril, peace be upon him, stands before Allah, the Exalted, his limbs trembling; Allah creates from every tremor a hundred thousand angels. So the angels are in rows before Allah, the Exalted, with their heads bowed. When Allah permits them to speak, they say: 'There is no god but You.' This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows; none shall speak except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted to speak, and he says what is right﴾," meaning the words: "There is no god but You."

The third: Ibn 'Abbas narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: [The Spirit in this verse is a host of the hosts of Allah, the Exalted. They are not angels; they have heads, hands, and feet, and they eat food.] Then he recited: ﴿On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows﴾, meaning these are a host and those are a host. This is the view of Abu Salih and Mujahid. According to this view, they are a creation in the form of the children of Adam, like people but not people.

The fourth: they are the noblest of the angels. This was said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

The fifth: they are guardians over the angels. This was said by Ibn Abi Najih.

The sixth: they are the children of Adam. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. So the meaning is "those possessing spirits" (dhawu al-ruh). Al-'Awfi and al-Qurazi said: "This is something Ibn 'Abbas used to conceal. He said: 'The Spirit is a creation of Allah's creation in the forms of the children of Adam, and no angel descends from the heaven without being accompanied by one of the Spirit.'"

The seventh: the spirits of the children of Adam will stand in a row, and the angels will stand in a row, and that is between the two blasts, before they are returned to the bodies. This was said by 'Atiyyah.

The eighth: it is the Qur'an. This was said by Zayd ibn Aslam, who recited: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit by Our command﴾.

(صَفًّا) is a verbal noun (masdar), meaning they will stand in rows (صُفُوفًا). A verbal noun may refer to the singular and the plural, like (العَدْل) and (الصَّوْم). The day of the festival is called "the Day of the Row" (يوم الصف). He said in another place: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, row upon row﴾ [al-Fajr: 22]. This indicates rows, and this is the time of the presentation and the reckoning. Al-Qutabi and others said this. It was also said: the Spirit stands in one row and the angels in another, so they are two rows. It was also said: all of them stand in one row. (لا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ), meaning they will not intercede except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted in intercession, and (وَقَالَ صَوَابًا), meaning "what is right," said al-Dahhak and Mujahid. Abu Salih said: "There is no god but Allah." al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "They will intercede for whoever said: 'There is no god but Allah.'"

The root of (الصَّوَاب) is correctness (السَّدَاد) in speech and action. It is from (أَصَابَ يُصِيبُ إِصَابَةً), like (الجَوَاب) from (أَجَابَ يُجِيبُ إِجَابَةً). It was also said: (لَا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ), meaning the angels and the Spirit who stood in rows, will not speak out of awe and reverence, except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted in intercession. And they have spoken what is right, for they affirm the oneness of Allah, the Exalted, and glorify Him. Al-Hasan said: "On the Day of Resurrection the Spirit will say: 'No one enters Paradise except by mercy, and no one enters the Fire except by deeds.'" This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and he says what is right﴾.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is the true day﴾, meaning the day that is certain and will occur. ﴿So whoever wills, let him take a way to his Lord as a return﴾, meaning a place of return through righteous deeds, as if when he does good he brings himself back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and when he does evil he removes himself from Him. This meaning is reflected in His saying, peace be upon him: [And all good is in Your hands, and evil is not attributed to You]. Qatadah said: (مَآبًا) means a way (سَبِيلًا).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾. It addresses the disbelievers of Quraysh and the polytheists of the Arabs, because they said: "We will not be resurrected." The punishment is the punishment of the Hereafter, and everything that is coming is near. Allah, Exalted is He, has said: ﴿As if, on the day they see it, they had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46]. al-Kalbi and others said this. Qatadah said: it is the punishment of this world, because it is the nearer of the two punishments. Muqatil said: it is the killing of Quraysh at Badr. The more apparent view is that it is the punishment of the Hereafter, which is death and the Resurrection, because whoever dies has had his resurrection. If he is among the people of Paradise, he sees his seat in Paradise; if he is among the people of the Fire, he sees disgrace and humiliation. This is why He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿On the day when a man will see what his hands have sent forth﴾.

[He specified the time of that punishment, meaning: We have warned you of a near punishment on that day, which is the day when a man will see what his hands have sent forth, meaning he will see it.] It was also said: "he looks at what he has sent forth," so the preposition (إِلَى) was omitted. (الْمَرْءُ) here, according to al-Hasan, means the believer, meaning he finds for himself a deed. As for the disbeliever, he finds no deed for himself, so he wishes he were dust. When He said: ﴿the disbeliever says﴾, it became known that He meant the believer by (الْمَرْءُ). It was also said: (الْمَرْءُ) here refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf and 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'it. The disbeliever in ﴿the disbeliever says﴾ is Abu Jahl. It was also said: it is general for every person who, on that day, sees the recompense for what he earned.

Muqatil said: the verse ﴿on the day when a man will see what his hands have sent forth﴾ was revealed concerning Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi, and ﴿the disbeliever says: "Would that I were dust!"﴾ was revealed concerning his brother al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Asad.

Al-Tha'labi said: "I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: 'The disbeliever here is Iblis, because he criticized Adam for being created from dust, and boasted that he was created from fire. When on the Day of Resurrection he sees what Adam and his children have of reward, ease, and mercy, and sees what he is in of hardship and punishment, he wishes he were in Adam's place, so he says: "Would that I were dust!"'" He said: "I saw this in one of the tafsir books of al-Qushayri, Abu Nasr." It was also said: meaning Iblis says: "Would that I had been created from dust and had not said, 'I am better than Adam.'"

Ibn 'Umar narrated: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be stretched like a hide, and the beasts, cattle, and wild animals will be gathered. Then retaliation will be established among the animals, until the hornless sheep is avenged against the horned sheep by its butting. When the retaliation among them is finished, it will be said to them: 'Become dust!' At that point the disbeliever says: 'Would that I were dust!'" Something similar is narrated from Abu Hurayrah and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with them. We have mentioned it in our book al-Tadhkirah, concerning the states of the dead and the affairs of the Hereafter, in an excellent manner, and praise be to Allah.

Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas mentioned: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Nafi' told us, who said: Salamah ibn Shabib told us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq told us, who said: Ma'mar told us, who said: Ja'far ibn Burqan al-Jazari informed me, on the authority of Yazid ibn al-Asamm, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Indeed Allah, Exalted is He, will gather all creation, every beast, bird, and human. Then it will be said to the cattle and the birds: 'Become dust!' At that point the disbeliever says: 'Would that I were dust!'"

Others said: ﴿Would that I were dust!﴾, meaning: "I was not resurrected," as He said: ﴿Would that I had not been given my record﴾ [al-Haqqah: 25]. Abu al-Zinad said: "When judgment has been passed among the people, and the people of Paradise have been commanded to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire, it will be said to the rest of the nations and to the believing jinn: 'Return to dust!' So they return to dust, and at that point the disbeliever, seeing them, says: 'Would that I were dust!'" Layth ibn Abi Sulaym said: "The believing jinn return to dust." 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, al-Zuhri, al-Kalbi, and Mujahid said: "The believing jinn are around Paradise, in its outskirts and courtyards, and they are not within it." This view is the most sound. Its explanation has already passed in surah al-Rahman [see vol. 17, p. 169], and that they are under obligation: they are rewarded and punished, so they are like the children of Adam. And Allah knows best what is correct.
